brief.text:
Meridian's promo desk looks buttoned up. You submit a callsign, it either takes it or spits back whatever the back office grumbled - word for word. Nobody thought to gag the back office.

Here's the play. Hand it a callsign that's already been claimed - a house name like ADMIN - and the machine chokes on the duplicate. In the middle of choking, it'll blurt out the name of the drawer it keeps those claims in. A drawer that's on none of our maps.

Make it complain. Read what it lets slip.
brief.objective: Force a duplicate error so the desk names the hidden table it stores claims in.

debrief.explanation: Two mistakes stacked on top of each other: the desk builds its SQL by concatenation, AND it forwards the database's raw complaint straight to you. Submit a callsign that already exists and SQLite refuses the duplicate with 'UNIQUE constraint failed: promo_claims.callsign' - a message that names the exact table and column you were never shown. The error itself is the leak. HONEST NOTE: SQLite leaks STRUCTURE this way (identifiers - table and column names), not row data. The classic MySQL version of this technique goes further, abusing functions like extractvalue()/updatexml() to smuggle actual DATA into the error text; SQLite has no such trick, so it won't spill row contents through errors. But a verbose error is still a free map of your schema.

debrief.takeaway: Never let the back office talk to the customer. Log the real error, hand back a shrug - and parameterize, because a verbose error is a free map of your schema.

database.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE promotions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT, active INTEGER); CREATE TABLE promo_claims (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, callsign TEXT UNIQUE, reward TEXT);
database.seedSql: INSERT INTO promotions (title,active) VALUES ('Summer Access Pass',1),('Founders Reward',0); INSERT INTO promo_claims (callsign,reward) VALUES ('ADMIN','house'),('FIXER','house'),('MERIDIAN','house');

query.description: Reserve a promo callsign (raw DB errors are shown to the user)

winCondition.reason: The desk choked and named its own hidden drawer: promo_claims. The error was the leak.

hints.text: A form that shows you the database's own complaint is a form that will tell on itself. You don't need it to succeed - you need it to FAIL loudly. Feed it something it has to reject.

The desk enforces unique callsigns. Submit one that's already taken and the database refuses the duplicate - and its refusal names the table.column it enforced the rule on. House names like ADMIN are always reserved.
Type  ADMIN  and submit. The response is 'UNIQUE constraint failed: promo_claims.callsign' - there's the hidden table (promo_claims) and its column, confessed by the error itself.

expectedSolution.note: ADMIN is already claimed, so the INSERT trips SQLite's UNIQUE constraint and the raw error names the hidden table promo_claims. A fresh callsign (e.g. NOVA-77) inserts cleanly and reveals nothing; a different error (e.g. a value-count mismatch) is not the targeted confession.
